game_text.4: A device for catching wild Pokémon. It is thrown like a ball at the target. It is designed as a capsule system.

Poké Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon.

game_text.3: A special BALL that is used only in the SAFARI ZONE.
game_text.4: A special Poké Ball that is used only in the Great Marsh. It is decorated in a camouflage pattern.

Safari Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon in the Great Marsh or Safari Zone. Success rate is 1.5×.

game_text.3: A BALL that works well on WATER- and BUG-type Pokémon.
game_text.4: A somewhat different Poké Ball that works especially well on Water- and Bug-type Pokémon.

Net Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate is 3× for water and bug Pokémon.

game_text.3: A BALL that works better on Pokémon on the ocean floor.
game_text.4: A somewhat different Poké Ball that works especially well on Pokémon that live in the sea.

Dive Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate is 3.5× when underwater, fishing, or surfing.

game_text.3: A BALL that works better on weaker Pokémon.
game_text.4: A somewhat different Poké Ball that works especially well on weaker Pokémon in the wild.

Nest Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate is 3.9× for level 1 Pokémon, and drops steadily to 1× at level 30.

game_text.3: A BALL that works better on Pokémon caught before.
game_text.4: A somewhat different Poké Ball that works especially well on Pokémon species that were previously caught.

Repeat Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate is 3× for previously-caught Pokémon.

game_text.3: A BALL that gains power in battles taking many turns.
game_text.4: A somewhat different Ball that becomes progressively better the more turns there are in a battle.

Timer Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate increases by 0.1× (Gen V: 0.3×) every turn, to a max of 4×.

game_text.3: A cozy BALL that makes Pokémon more friendly.
game_text.4: A comfortable Poké Ball that makes a caught wild Pokémon quickly grow friendly.

Luxury Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Caught Pokémon start with 200 happiness.

game_text.3: A rare BALL made in commemoration of some event.
game_text.4: A somewhat rare Poké Ball that has been specially made to commemorate an event of some sort.

Premier Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon.

game_text.4: A somewhat different Poké Ball that makes it easier to catch wild Pokémon at night or in dark places like caves.

Dusk Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate is 3.5× at night and in caves.

game_text.4: A remedial Poké Ball that restores the caught Pokémon’s HP and eliminates any status problem.

Heal Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Caught Pokémon are immediately healed.

game_text.4: A somewhat different Poké Ball that provides a better catch rate if it is used at the start of a wild encounter.

Quick Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon. Success rate is 4× (Gen V: 5×), but only on the first turn.

game_text.4: A quite rare Poké Ball that has been specially crafted to commemorate an occasion of some sort.

Cherish Ball.summary: Tries to catch a wild Pokémon.

game_text.3: Restores the HP of a Pokémon by 20 points.
game_text.4: A spray-type medicine for wounds. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by just 20 points.

game_text.3: Heals a paralyzed Pokémon.

game_text.3: Fully restores the HP and status of a Pokémon.

game_text.3: Fully restores the HP of a Pokémon.
game_text.4: A spray-type medicine for wounds. It completely restores the HP of a single Pokémon.

game_text.3: Restores the HP of a Pokémon by 200 points.
game_text.4: A spray-type medicine for wounds. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 200 points.

game_text.3: Restores the HP of a Pokémon by 50 points.

Full Heal.summary: Cures any status ailment and confusion.

game_text.3: Revives a fainted Pokémon with half its HP.
game_text.4: A medicine that revives a fainted Pokémon. It restores half the Pokémon’s maximum HP.

game_text.3: Revives a fainted Pokémon with all its HP.
game_text.4: A medicine that revives a fainted Pokémon. It fully restores the Pokémon’s HP.

game_text.3: A mineral water that restores HP by 50 points.
game_text.4: Water with a high mineral content. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 50 points.

game_text.3: A fizzy soda drink that restores HP by 60 points.
game_text.4: A fizzy soda drink. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 60 points.

game_text.3: A very sweet drink that restores HP by 80 points.
game_text.4: A very sweet drink. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 80 points.

game_text.3: A nutritious milk that restores HP by 100 points.
game_text.4: Milk with a very high nutrition content. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 100 points.

game_text.3: A bitter powder that restores HP by 50 points.
game_text.4: A very bitter medicine powder. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 50 points.

game_text.3: A bitter root that restores HP by 200 points.
game_text.4: A very bitter root. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by 200 points.

game_text.3: A bitter powder that heals all status problems.
game_text.4: A very bitter medicine powder. It heals all the status problems of a single Pokémon.

Heal Powder.summary: Cures any status ailment, but lowers happiness.

game_text.3: A very bitter herb that revives a fainted Pokémon.
game_text.4: A very bitter medicinal herb. It revives a fainted Pokémon, fully restoring its HP.

Revival Herb.summary: Revives with full HP, but lowers happiness.

game_text.3: Restores the PP of a selected move by 10.
game_text.4: It restores the PP of a Pokémon’s selected move by a maximum of 10 points.

game_text.3: Fully restores the PP of a selected move.
game_text.4: It fully restores the PP of a single selected move that has been learned by the target Pokémon.

Max Ether.summary: Restores PP to full for one move.

game_text.3: Fully restores the PP of a Pokémon’s moves.
game_text.4: It fully restores the PP of all the moves learned by the targeted Pokémon.

Max Elixir.summary: Restores PP to full for each move.

game_text.3: A local specialty that heals all status problems.
game_text.4: Lavaridge Town’s local specialty. It heals all the status problems of one Pokémon.

Lava Cookie.summary: Cures any status ailment and confusion.

game_text.3: A 100% pure juice that restores HP by 20 points.
game_text.4: A 100% pure juice made of Berries. It restores the HP of one Pokémon by just 20 points.

game_text.3: Fully revives and restores all fainted Pokémon.
game_text.4: It revives all fainted Pokémon. In doing so, it also fully restores their HP.

Sacred Ash.summary: Revives all fainted Pokémon with full HP.

game_text.3: Raises the base HP of one Pokémon.
game_text.4: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. It raises the base HP of a single Pokémon.

game_text.3: Raises the base ATTACK stat of one Pokémon.
game_text.4: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. It raises the base Attack stat of a single Pokémon.

game_text.3: Raises the base DEFENSE stat of one Pokémon.
game_text.4: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. It raises the base Defense stat of a single Pokémon.

game_text.3: Raises the base SPEED stat of one Pokémon.
game_text.4: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. It raises the base Speed stat of a single Pokémon.

game_text.3: Raises the base SP. ATK stat of one Pokémon.
game_text.4: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. It raises the base Sp. Atk (Special Attack) stat of a single Pokémon.

Calcium.summary: Raises Special Attack effort and happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the level of a Pokémon by one.
game_text.4: A candy that is packed with energy. It raises the level of a single Pokémon by one.

Rare Candy.summary: Causes a level-up and raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the maximum PP of a selected move.
game_text.4: It slightly raises the maximum PP of a selected move that has been learned by the target Pokémon.

PP Up.summary: Raises a move’s max PP by 20%.

game_text.3: Raises the base SP. DEF stat of one Pokémon.
game_text.4: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. It raises the base Sp. Def (Special Defense) stat of a single Pokémon.

game_text.3: Raises the PP of a move to its maximum points.
game_text.4: It maximally raises the top PP of a selected move that has been learned by the target Pokémon.

PP Max.summary: Raises a move’s max PP by 60%.

game_text.4: Old Chateau’s hidden specialty. It heals all the status problems of a single Pokémon.

Old Gateau.summary: Cures any status ailment and confusion.

game_text.3: Prevents stat reduction when used in battle.
game_text.4: An item that prevents stat reduction among the Trainer’s party Pokémon for five turns after use.

Guard Spec..summary: Prevents stat changes in battle for five turns in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the critical-hit ratio during one battle.
game_text.4: An item that raises the critical-hit ratio of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

Dire Hit.summary: Increases the chance of a critical hit in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the stat ATTACK during one battle.
game_text.4: An item that raises the Attack stat of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

X Attack.summary: Raises Attack by one stage in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the stat DEFENSE during one battle.
game_text.4: An item that raises the Defense stat of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

X Defense.summary: Raises Defense by one stage in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the stat SPEED during one battle.
game_text.4: An item that raises the Speed stat of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

X Speed.summary: Raises Speed by one stage in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises accuracy of attack moves during one battle.
game_text.4: An item that raises the accuracy of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

X Accuracy.summary: Raises accuracy by one stage in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Raises the stat SP. ATK during one battle.
game_text.4: An item that raises the Sp. Atk stat of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

X Sp. Atk.summary: Raises Special Attack by one stage in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.4: An item that raises the Sp. Def stat of a Pokémon in battle. It wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

X Sp. Def.summary: Raises Special Defense by one stage in battle. Raises happiness.

game_text.3: Use to flee from any battle with a wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: A doll that attracts Pokémon. Use it to flee from any battle with a wild Pokémon.

game_text.3: Use to flee from any battle with a wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: An item that attracts Pokémon. Use it to flee from any battle with a wild Pokémon.

game_text.3: A glass flute that awakens sleeping Pokémon.
game_text.4: A blue flute made from blown glass. Its melody awakens a single Pokémon from sleep.

game_text.3: A glass flute that snaps Pokémon out of confusion.
game_text.4: A yellow flute made from blown glass. Its melody snaps a single Pokémon out of confusion.

game_text.3: A glass flute that snaps Pokémon out of attraction.
game_text.4: A red flute made from blown glass. Its melody snaps a single Pokémon out of infatuation.

game_text.3: A glass flute that keeps away wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: A black flute made from blown glass. Its melody makes wild Pokémon less likely to appear.

Black Flute.summary: Halves the wild Pokémon encounter rate.

game_text.3: A glass flute that lures wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: A white flute made from blown glass. Its melody makes wild Pokémon more likely to appear.

White Flute.summary: Doubles the wild Pokémon encounter rate.

game_text.3: Salt obtained from deep inside the SHOAL CAVE.
game_text.4: Pure salt that was discovered deep inside the Shoal Cave. It is extremely salty.

Shoal Salt.summary: No effect. Gen III: Trade four and four Shoal Shells for a Shell Bell.

game_text.3: A seashell found deep inside the SHOAL CAVE.
game_text.4: A pretty seashell that was found deep inside the Shoal Cave. It is striped in blue and white.

Shoal Shell.summary: No effect. Gen III: Trade four and four Shoal Salts for a Shell Bell.

game_text.3: A shard from an ancient item. Can be sold cheaply.
game_text.4: A small red shard. It appears to be from some sort of implement made long ago.

Red Shard.summary: No effect. Can be traded for items or moves.

game_text.3: A shard from an ancient item. Can be sold cheaply.
game_text.4: A small blue shard. It appears to be from some sort of implement made long ago.

Blue Shard.summary: No effect. Can be traded for items or moves.

game_text.3: A shard from an ancient item. Can be sold cheaply.
game_text.4: A small yellow shard. It appears to be from some sort of implement made long ago.

Yellow Shard.summary: No effect. Can be traded for items or moves.

game_text.4: A small green shard. It appears to be from some sort of implement made long ago.

Green Shard.summary: No effect. Can be traded for items or moves.

game_text.3: Repels weak wild Pokémon for 200 steps.
game_text.4: An item that prevents weak wild Pokémon from appearing for 200 steps after its use.

Super Repel.summary: For 200 steps, prevents wild encounters of level lower than your party’s lead Pokémon.

game_text.3: Repels weak wild Pokémon for 250 steps.
game_text.4: An item that prevents weak wild Pokémon from appearing for 250 steps after its use.

Max Repel.summary: For 250 steps, prevents wild encounters of level lower than your party’s lead Pokémon.

game_text.3: Use to escape instantly from a cave or a dungeon.
game_text.4: A long, durable rope. Use it to escape instantly from a cave or a dungeon.

Escape Rope.summary: Transports user to the outside entrance of a cave.

game_text.3: Repels weak wild Pokémon for 100 steps.
game_text.4: An item that prevents weak wild Pokémon from appearing for 100 steps after its use.

Repel.summary: For 100 steps, prevents wild encounters of level lower than your party’s lead Pokémon.

game_text.3: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is as red as the sun.

Sun Stone.summary: Evolves a Cottonee into Whimsicott, a Gloom into Bellossom, a Petilil into Lilligant, or a Sunkern into Sunflora.

game_text.3: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is as black as the night sky.

Moon Stone.summary: Evolves a Clefairy into Clefable, a Jigglypuff into Wigglytuff, a Munna into Musharna, a Nidorina into Nidoqueen, a Nidorino into Nidoking, or a Skitty into Delcatty.

game_text.3: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is colored orange.

Fire Stone.summary: Evolves an Eevee into Flareon, a Growlithe into Arcanine, a Pansear into Simisear, or a Vulpix into Ninetales.

game_text.3: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It has a thunderbolt pattern.

Thunder Stone.summary: Evolves an Eelektrik into Eelektross, an Eevee into Jolteon, or a Pikachu into Raichu.

game_text.3: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is a clear, light blue.

Water Stone.summary: Evolves an Eevee into Vaporeon, a Lombre into Ludicolo, a Panpour into Simipour, a Poliwhirl into Poliwrath, a Shellder into Cloyster, or a Staryu into Starmie.

game_text.3: Makes certain species of Pokémon evolve.
game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It has a leaf pattern.

Leaf Stone.summary: Evolves an Exeggcute into Exeggutor, a Gloom into Vileplume, a Nuzleaf into Shiftry, a Pansage into Simisage, or a Weepinbell into Victreebel.

game_text.3: A plain mushroom that would sell at a cheap price.
game_text.4: A small and rare mushroom. It is quite popular among certain maniacal fan segments.

Tiny Mushroom.summary: Fire Red and Leaf Green: Trade two for prior Level-up moves. Sell for 250 Pokédollars, or to Hungry Maid for 500 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: A rare mushroom that would sell at a high price.
game_text.4: A large and rare mushroom. It is very popular among certain maniacal fan segments.

Big Mushroom.summary: Fire Red and Leaf Green: Trade for prior Level-up moves. Sell for 2500 Pokédollars, or to Hungry Maid for 5000 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: A pretty pearl that would sell at a cheap price.
game_text.4: A somewhat-small pearl that sparkles in a pretty silver color. It can be sold cheaply to shops.

Pearl.summary: Sell for 700 Pokédollars, or to Ore Collector for 1400 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: A lovely large pearl that would sell at a high price.
game_text.4: A quite-large pearl that sparkles in a pretty silver color. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

Big Pearl.summary: Sell for 3750 Pokédollars, or to Ore Collector for 7500 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: Beautiful red sand. Can be sold at a high price.
game_text.4: Lovely, red-colored sand with a loose, silky feel. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

Stardust.summary: Sell for 1000 Pokédollars, or to Ore Collector for 2000 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: A red gem shard. It would sell for a very high price.
game_text.4: A shard of a pretty gem that sparkles in a red color. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

Star Piece.summary: Platinum: Trade for one of each color Shard. Black and White: Trade for PP Up. Sell for 4900 Pokédollars, or to Ore Collector for 9800 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: A nugget of pure gold. Can be sold at a high price.
game_text.4: A nugget of pure gold that gives off a lustrous gleam. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

Nugget.summary: Sell for 5000 Pokédollars, or to Ore Collector for 10000 Pokédollars.

game_text.3: A lovely scale. It is coveted by collectors.
game_text.4: A pretty, heart-shaped scale that is extremely rare. It glows faintly in the colors of the rainbow.

Heart Scale.summary: No effect. Can be traded for prior Level-up moves.

game_text.4: A sweet honey with a lush aroma that attracts wild Pokémon when it is used in grass, caves, or on special trees.
A fertilizer to be spread on soft soil. It speeds up the growth of Berries. However, it also dries the soil faster.

Growth Mulch.summary: Growing time of berries is reduced, but the soil dries out faster.

game_text.4: A fertilizer to be spread on soft soil. It slows the growth of Berries and causes the soil to dry slower.

Damp Mulch.summary: Growing time of berries is increased, but the soil dries out slower.

game_text.4: A fertilizer to be spread on soft soil. It extends the time ripened Berries remain on their plants before falling.

Stable Mulch.summary: Berries stay on the plant for longer than their usual time.

game_text.4: A fertilizer to be spread on soft soil. It ups the number of times new plants grow where mature plants withered.

Gooey Mulch.summary: Berries regrow from dead plants an increased number of times.

game_text.3: A fossil of an ancient, seafloor- dwelling Pokémon.
game_text.4: A fossil of an ancient Pokémon that lived in the sea. It appears to be part of a plant root.

Root Fossil.summary: Can be revived into a Lileep.

game_text.3: A fossil of an ancient, seafloor- dwelling Pokémon.
game_text.4: A fossil of an ancient Pokémon that lived in the sea. It appears to be part of a claw.

Claw Fossil.summary: Can be revived into an Anorith.

game_text.3: A piece of an ancient marine Pokémon’s seashell.
game_text.4: A fossil of an ancient Pokémon that lived in the sea. It appears to be part of a seashell.

Helix Fossil.summary: Can be revived into an Omanyte.

game_text.3: A piece of an ancient marine Pokémon’s shell.
game_text.4: A fossil of an ancient Pokémon that lived in the sea. It appears to be part of a shell.

Dome Fossil.summary: Can be revived into a Kabuto.

game_text.3: A stone containing the genes of an ancient Pokémon.
game_text.4: A piece of amber that contains the genetic material of an ancient Pokémon. It is clear with a reddish tint.

Old Amber.summary: Can be revived into an Aerodactyl.

game_text.4: A fossil from a prehistoric Pokémon that lived on the land. It appears to be part of a collar.

Armor Fossil.summary: Can be revived into a Shieldon.

game_text.4: A fossil from a prehistoric Pokémon that lived on the land. It appears to be part of a head.

Skull Fossil.summary: Can be revived into a Cranidos.

game_text.4: A bone that is extremely valuable for Pokémon archaeology. It can be sold for a high price to shops.

Rare Bone.summary: Sell for 5000 Pokédollars, or to Bone Man for 10000 Pokédollars.

game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It shines with a dazzling light.

Shiny Stone.summary: Evolves a Minccino into Cinccino, a Roselia into Roserade, or a Togetic into Togekiss.

game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is as dark as dark can be.

Dusk Stone.summary: Evolves a Lampent into Chandelure, a Misdreavus into Mismagius, or a Murkrow into Honchkrow.

game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It sparkles like eyes.

Dawn Stone.summary: Evolves a male Kirlia into Gallade or a female Snorunt into Froslass.

game_text.4: A peculiar stone that makes certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is shaped like an egg.

Oval Stone.summary: Level-up during Day on a Happiny: Holder evolves into Chansey.

game_text.4: A vital item that is needed to keep a stone tower from collapsing. Voices can be heard from it occasionally.

Odd Keystone.summary: Use on the tower on Route 209 to encounter Spiritomb if you have at least 32 Underground greetings.

game_text.4: A brightly gleaming orb to be held by DIALGA. It boosts the power of Dragon-​ and Steel-type moves.

Adamant Orb.summary: Boosts the damage from Dialga’s Dragon-type and Steel-type moves by 20%.

game_text.4: A beautifully glowing orb to be held by PALKIA. It boosts the power of Dragon-​ and Water-type moves.

Lustrous Orb.summary: Boosts the damage from Palkia’s Dragon-type and Water-type moves by 20%.

game_text.4: The user endures any attack, leaving 1 HP. Its chance of failing rises if it is used in succession.

TM58.summary: Teaches Sky Drop to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Endure)

game_text.4: The foe is attacked with a shock wave generated by the user’s gaping mouth.

TM59.summary: Teaches Incinerate to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Dragon Pulse)

game_text.4: An energy-draining punch. The user’s HP is restored by half the damage taken by the target.

TM60.summary: Teaches Quash to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Drain Punch)

game_text.4: The user shoots a sinister, bluish white flame at the foe to inflict a burn.

TM61.summary: Teaches Will-O-Wisp to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The foe is attacked with powdery scales blown by wind. It may also raise all the user’s stats.

TM62.summary: Teaches Acrobatics to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Silver Wind)

game_text.4: It prevents the foe from using its held item. Its Trainer is also prevented from using items on it.

TM63.summary: Teaches Embargo to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user explodes to inflict damage on all Pokémon in battle. The user faints upon using this move.

TM64.summary: Teaches Explosion to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user slashes with a sharp claw made from shadows. It has a high critical-hit ratio.

TM65.summary: Teaches Shadow Claw to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user stores power, then attacks. If the user can use this attack after the foe, its power is doubled.

TM66.summary: Teaches Payback to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user recycles a single-use item that has been used in battle so it can be used again.

TM67.summary: Teaches Retaliate to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Recycle)

game_text.4: The user charges the foe using every bit of its power. It must rest on the next turn to recover.

TM68.summary: Teaches Giga Impact to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user polishes its body to reduce drag. It sharply raises the Speed stat.

TM69.summary: Teaches Rock Polish to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user flashes a light that cuts the foe’s accuracy. It can also be used to illuminate caves.

TM70.summary: Teaches Flash to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user stabs the foe with a sharpened stone from below. It has a high critical-hit ratio.

TM71.summary: Teaches Stone Edge to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: An attack move that inflicts double the damage if the user has been hurt by the foe in the same turn.

TM72.summary: Teaches Volt Switch to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Avalanche)

game_text.4: A weak electric charge is launched at the foe. It causes paralysis if it hits.

TM73.summary: Teaches Thunder Wave to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user tackles the foe from a high-speed spin. The slower the user, the greater the damage.

TM74.summary: Teaches Gyro Ball to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: A frenetic dance to uplift the fighting spirit. It sharply raises the user’s Attack stat.

TM75.summary: Teaches Swords Dance to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user lays a trap of levitating stones around the foe. The trap hurts foes that switch into battle.

TM76.summary: Teaches Struggle Bug to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Stealth Rock)

game_text.4: The user hypnotizes itself into copying any stat change made by the foe.

TM77.summary: Teaches Psych Up to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: If it is the opposite gender of the user, the foe is charmed into sharply lowering its Sp. Atk stat.

TM78.summary: Teaches Bulldoze to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Captivate)

game_text.4: The user releases a horrible aura imbued with dark thoughts. It may also make the target flinch.

TM79.summary: Teaches Frost Breath to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Dark Pulse)

game_text.4: Large boulders are hurled at the foe to inflict damage. It may also make the target flinch.

TM80.summary: Teaches Rock Slide to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user slashes at the foe by crossing its scythes or claws as if they were a pair of scissors.

TM81.summary: Teaches X-Scissor to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: While it is asleep, the user randomly uses one of the moves it knows.

TM82.summary: Teaches Dragon Tail to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Sleep Talk)

game_text.4: The user draws power from the Berry it is holding to attack. The Berry determines its type and power.

TM83.summary: Teaches Work Up to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Natural Gift)

game_text.4: The foe is stabbed with a tentacle or arm steeped with poison. It may also poison the foe.

TM84.summary: Teaches Poison Jab to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: An attack that works only on a sleeping foe. It absorbs half the damage caused to heal the user’s HP.

TM85.summary: Teaches Dream Eater to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user snares the foe with grass and trips it. The heavier the foe, the greater the damage.

TM86.summary: Teaches Grass Knot to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user enrages the foe into confusion. However, it also sharply raises the foe’s Attack stat.

TM87.summary: Teaches Swagger to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user pecks the foe. If the foe is holding a Berry, the user plucks it and gains its effect.

TM88.summary: Teaches Pluck to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: After making its attack, the user rushes back to switch places with a party Pokémon in waiting.

TM89.summary: Teaches U-turn to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user makes a copy of itself using some of its HP. The copy serves as the user’s decoy.

TM90.summary: Teaches Substitute to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user gathers all its light energy and releases it in one shot. It may also lower the foe’s Sp. Def stat.

TM91.summary: Teaches Flash Cannon to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.4: The user creates a bizarre space in which slower Pokémon get to move first for five turns.

TM92.summary: Teaches Trick Room to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.3: Attacks the foe with sharp blades or claws.
game_text.4: The foe is cut with a scythe or a claw. It can also be used to cut down thin trees.

HM01.summary: Teaches Cut to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.3: Flies up on the first turn, then attacks next turn.
game_text.4: The user soars, then strikes on the second turn. It can also be used to fly to any familiar town.

HM02.summary: Teaches Fly to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.3: Creates a huge wave, then crashes it down on the foe.
game_text.4: It swamps the entire battlefield with a giant wave. It can also be used to cross water.

HM03.summary: Teaches Surf to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.3: Builds enormous power, then slams the foe.
game_text.4: The foe is slugged with a punch thrown at maximum power. It can also be used to move boulders.

HM04.summary: Teaches Strength to a compatible Pokémon.

game_text.3: Looses a powerful blast of light that reduces accuracy.
game_text.4: Traps foes in a violent swirling whirlpool. It can also be used to traverse whirlpools.

HM05.summary: Teaches Waterfall to a compatible Pokémon. (HS: Whirlpool DPP: Defog Gen III & II & I: Flash)

game_text.3: A rock-crushingly tough attack that may lower DEFENSE.
game_text.4: The user slugs the foe with a shattering punch. It can also smash cracked boulders.

HM06.summary: Teaches Dive to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV & III: Rock Smash Gen II: Whirlpool)

game_text.3: Attacks the foe with enough power to climb waterfalls.
game_text.4: The user charges the foe at an awesome speed. It can also be used to climb a waterfall.

HM07.summary: Teaches a move to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV & III & II: Waterfall)

game_text.3: Dives underwater the 1st turn, then attacks next turn.
game_text.4: A charging attack that may also leave the foe confused. It can also be used to scale rocky walls.

HM08.summary: Teaches a move to a compatible Pokémon. (Gen IV: Rock Climb Gen III: Dive)

game_text.4: A bag filled with convenient tools for exploring. It provides access to the Underground.
A sturdy, spacious bag that is used to carry loot obtained in the coal mine.
It lists the rules for holding battles. For linked battles, you may choose which set of rules you wish to use.

Rule Book.summary: List of battle types and their rules.

game_text.4: A tool that can search out Pokémon that are hiding in grass. Its battery is recharged as you walk.

Poké Radar.summary: Use to track down rare or shiny Pokémon. 50 steps to recharge.

game_text.4: A card that lists the Battle Points you have earned.

Point Card.summary: Keeps count of Battle Points earned.

game_text.4: A notebook that keeps a day-to-day record of your adventure so far.

Journal.summary: Records prior significant activities the player took.

game_text.4: A case for storing Seals that can be applied to the Capsule cases of Poké Balls.

Seal Case.summary: Stores Seals that can be applied to Poké Ball capsules.

game_text.4: A fancy case for the tidy arrangement and storage of whimsical Pokémon Accessories.

Fashion Case.summary: Holds Pokémon Accessories for use in Contests.

game_text.4: A tiny bag that can hold ten Seals for decorating Poké Balls.

Seal Bag.summary: Holds ten Seals for Poké Balls.

game_text.4: A convenient notepad that is used for registering your friends, Friend Codes, and keeping a record of game play.

Pal Pad.summary: Use to record Friend Codes and check your own.

game_text.4: A large key for operating the doors of the Valley Windworks in the canyon. It was held by a Team Galactic Grunt.
An ancient good-luck charm made of Pokémon bones to be taken to the elder of Celestic Town.

Old Charm.summary: Trade to Cynthia’s grandmother in Celestic Town for HM04 (Surf).

game_text.4: A card key for disengaging security systems in the Galactic HQ. Losing it can result in punishment, apparently.

Galactic Key.summary: Grants access to Galactic HQ in Veilstone City.

game_text.4: A mythical chain that is said to link the legendary Pokémon that created the Sinnoh region.

Red Chain.summary: Used to bind Palkia and Dialga.

game_text.3: Can be viewed anytime. Shows your present location.
game_text.4: A very convenient map that can be viewed anytime. It even shows your present location.

Town Map.summary: Use to see the overworld map.

game_text.3: A rechargeable unit that flags battle- ready TRAINERS.
game_text.4: A device that indicates Trainers who want to battle. Its battery charges while you walk.

Vs. Seeker.summary: Allows rebattling of on-screen trainers. 100 steps to recharge.

game_text.3: A case that holds up to 9,999 COINS.
game_text.4: A case for holding coins obtained at the Game Corner. It holds up to 50,000 coins.

Coin Case.summary: Holds coins for the Game Corner.

game_text.3: Use by any body of water to fish for wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: An old and beat-up fishing rod. Use it by any body of water to fish for wild aquatic Pokémon.

Old Rod.summary: Used to catch Pokémon in bodies of water.

game_text.3: A decent fishing rod for catching wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: A new, good-quality fishing rod. Use it by any body of water to fish for wild aquatic Pokémon.

Good Rod.summary: Used to catch Pokémon in bodies of water.

game_text.3: The best fishing rod for catching wild Pokémon.
game_text.4: An awesome, high-tech fishing rod. Use it by any body of water to fish for wild aquatic Pokémon.

Super Rod.summary: Used to catch Pokémon in bodies of water.

game_text.4: A watering can shaped like a PSYDUCK. It helps promote healthy growth of Berries planted in soft soil.
A case for storing Poffin cooked from Berries.

game_text.3: A folding bicycle that is faster than the RUNNING SHOES.
game_text.4: A folding Bicycle that enables much faster movement than the Running Shoes.
A key to one of the suites at the luxury hotel by a lake. For some odd reason, it often disappears.

Suite Key.summary: Opens a locked building in the Lakeside Resort.

game_text.4: A letter from Prof. Oak. Written in it is a request for you to go to Rt. 224.

Oak’s Letter.summary: Allows access to Seabreak path, Flower Paradise, and Shaymin.

game_text.4: A feather that glows like the moon. It is said to possess the power to dispel nightmares.

Lunar Wing.summary: Cures sailor’s son of nightmares in Canalave City.

game_text.4: A card needed for entering the inn in Canalave City. Oddly, the last date marked on it was 50 years ago.

Member Card.summary: Allows access to Newmoon Island and Darkrai.

game_text.4: A flute that puts out echoing sounds that do not seem to be of this world. It is unknown who made it.

Azure Flute.summary: Allows entry into the Hall of Origin. Unreleased.

game_text.3: The ticket required for sailing on a ferry.
game_text.4: The ticket required for sailing on the ferry S.S. Aqua. It has a drawing of a ship on it.

S.S. Ticket.summary: Ticket for a ship. (RSE: S.S. Tidal LF: S.S. Anne HG: S.S. Aqua)

game_text.3: The pass required for entering Pokémon CONTESTS.
game_text.4: The pass required for entering Pokémon Contests. It has a drawing of an award ribbon on it.
A stone formed when boulders melted in intensely hot magma, then hardened. Magma remains sealed inside.
A parcel entrusted in your care. You are supposed to deliver it to your childhood friend who left Twinleaf Town.

Parcel.summary: Given to the trainer’s rival in Jubilife City. Contains Town Maps.

game_text.4: A coupon to be exchanged for a Pokémon Watch (Pokétch for short). Three coupons are needed.

Coupon 1.summary: The first of three tickets used to obtain a Pokétch.

game_text.4: A coupon to be exchanged for a Pokémon Watch (Pokétch for short). Three coupons are needed.

Coupon 2.summary: The second of three tickets used to obtain a Pokétch.

game_text.4: A coupon to be exchanged for a Pokémon Watch (Pokétch for short). Three coupons are needed.

Coupon 3.summary: The last of three tickets used to obtain a Pokétch.

game_text.3: The key to the storage inside the ABANDONED SHIP.
game_text.4: The key to Team Galactic’s sinister warehouse located at the edge of Veilstone City.

Storage Key.summary: Grants access to the Team Galactic warehouse in Veilstone City.

game_text.4: A fantastic medicine dispensed by the pharmacy in Cianwood City. It fully heals a Pokémon of any ailment.

Secret Potion.summary: Used to heal the Ampharos at the top of Olivine Lighthouse.

game_text.4: A glowing orb to be held by GIRATINA. It boosts the power of Dragon- and Ghost-type moves.

Griseous Orb.summary: Boosts the damage from Giratina’s Dragon-type and Ghost-type moves by 20%, and transforms it into Origin Forme.

game_text.4: An amazing device that can record a battle either between friends or at a special battle facility.

Vs. Recorder.summary: Records wireless, Wi-Fi, or Battle Frontier battles, and stores points.

game_text.4: A flower sometimes bundled in bouquets to convey gratitude on special occasions like birthdays.

Gracidea.summary: Changes an unfrozen Shaymin to Sky Forme in the day.

game_text.3: The key to the CINNABAR ISLAND GYM’s entrance.
game_text.4: A high-tech key that has to be used at a specific location. It emits a special electric signal to open a door.

Secret Key.summary: Gen IV: The key to Rotom’s appliance room. Gen III: The key to Cinnabar Gym.

game_text.4: A handy box where you can store up to 99 Apricorns of each kind.
Handy containers for cultivating Berries wherever you go.
A bottle used for watering plants in the Berry Pots.

Squirt Bottle.summary: Use on Sudowoodo blocking the path on Route 36. Also waters berries.

game_text.4: A Poké Ball for catching Pokémon hooked by a Rod when fishing.

Lure Ball.summary: 3× effectiveness while fishing. Made from Blu Apricorn.

game_text.4: A Poké Ball for catching Pokémon that are a lower level than your own.

Level Ball.summary: Success rate based off of fraction target Pokémon is of user’s Pokémon. Made from Red Apricorn.

game_text.4: A Poké Ball for catching Pokémon that evolve using the Moon Stone.

Moon Ball.summary: 4× effectiveness on familes of Pokémon with a Moon Stone evolution. Made from Ylw Apricorn.

game_text.4: A Poké Ball for catching very heavy Pokémon.

Heavy Ball.summary: Has flat bonus or penalty to catch rate depending on weight class of target. Made from Blk Apricorn.

game_text.4: A Poké Ball that makes it easier to catch fast Pokémon.

Fast Ball.summary: 4× effectiveness on Pokémon with 100 or greater base speed. (Gen II: Roaming or Fleeing Pokémon). Made from Wht Apricorn.

game_text.4: A Poké Ball that makes caught Pokémon more friendly.

Friend Ball.summary: Caught Pokémon start with 200 happiness. Made from Grn Apricorn.

game_text.4: Poké Ball for catching Pokémon that are the opposite gender of your Pokémon.

Love Ball.summary: 8× effectiveness on opposite sex, same species targets of the Active Pokémon. Made from Pnk Apricorn.

game_text.4: A special Poké Ball for the Pal Park.

Park Ball.summary: Catches Pokémon in the Pal Park every time.

game_text.4: A special Poké Ball for the Bug-Catching Contest.

Sport Ball.summary: Tries to catch a Pokémon in the Bug-Catching contest in National Park. (Gen II: Park Ball)

game_text.4: A red Apricorn. It assails your nostrils.

Red Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Level Ball.

game_text.4: A blue Apricorn. It smells a bit like grass.

Blue Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Lure Ball.

game_text.4: A yellow Apricorn. It has an invigorating scent.

Yellow Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Moon Ball.

game_text.4: A green Apricorn. It has a mysterious, aromatic scent.

Green Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Friend Ball.

game_text.4: A pink Apricorn. It has a nice, sweet scent.

Pink Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Love Ball.

game_text.4: A white Apricorn. It doesn’t smell like anything.

White Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Fast Ball.

game_text.4: A black Apricorn It has an indescribable scent.

Black Apricorn.summary: Used to make a Heavy Ball.

game_text.3: A device that signals an invisible item by sound.
game_text.4: It checks for unseen items in the area and makes noise and lights when it finds something.

Dowsing Machine.summary: Use to find hidden items on the field. AKA Itemfinder.

game_text.4: A famous candy in Mahogany Town. Many tourists like to buy them to take home.

Rage Candy Bar.summary: HS: Traded for TM64. Gen II & Gen V: Acts as a Potion.

game_text.3: A red, glowing orb said to contain an ancient power.
game_text.4: A shiny red orb that is said to have a legend and has a deep connection with the Hoenn region.

Red Orb.summary: Summons Groudon to the Embedded Tower.

game_text.3: A blue, glowing orb said to contain an ancient power.
game_text.4: A shiny blue orb that is said to have a legend and has a deep connection with the Hoenn region.

Blue Orb.summary: Summons Kyogre to the Embedded Tower.

game_text.4: A shiny green orb that is said to have a legend and has a deep connection with the Hoenn region.

Jade Orb.summary: Summons Rayquaza to the Embedded Tower.

game_text.4: A crystal ball that was excavated from the ground. A very beautiful stone that is covered with bits of rock and earth.

Enigma Stone.summary: S: Summons Latias H: Summons Latios.

game_text.4: A report of all the discovered kinds of UNOWN.

Unown Report.summary: Keeps track of Unown types caught.

game_text.4: A card to save points for the Buena’s Password show.

Blue Card.summary: Keeps track of points from Buena’s show.

game_text.4: A very tasty tail of something. It sells for a high price.

Slowpoke Tail.summary: A tasty tail that sells for a high price.

game_text.4: A very old-fashioned bell that makes a gentle ringing.

Clear Bell.summary: HS: Allows Kimono-girls to summon Ho-oh. C: Summons Suicune to the Tin Tower.

game_text.3: A card-type door key used in SILPH CO’s office.
game_text.4: A card key that opens a shutter in the Radio Tower.

Card Key.summary: HS: Opens doors in the Radio Tower. Gen III: Unlocks Silph Co Doors.

game_text.3: The key for NEW MAUVILLE beneath MAUVILLE CITY.
game_text.4: A key that opens a door in the Goldenrod Tunnel.

Basement Key.summary: HS: Key to the tunnel under Goldenrod City. Gen III: Key to New Mauville.

game_text.4: A scale from the red GYARADOS. It glows red like a flame.

Red Scale.summary: Trade to Mr. Pokémon for an Exp. Share.

game_text.4: The Poké Doll lost by the Copycat.

Lost Item.summary: A Poké Doll lost by the Copycat who lives in Saffron City. Trade for a Pass.

game_text.4: A ticket required for riding the Magnet Train. It allows you to ride whenever and however much you’d like.

Pass.summary: Grants access to ride the Magnet Train between Goldenrod City and Saffron City.

Machine Part.summary: Must be replaced in the Power Plant to power the Magnet Train.

game_text.4: A strange, silvery feather that sparkles.

Silver Wing.summary: Summons Lugia to the Whirl Islands.

game_text.4: A mystical, rainbow feather that sparkles.

Rainbow Wing.summary: Summons Ho-Oh at the top of the Bell Tower.

game_text.4: A mysterious Egg obtained from Mr. Pokémon. What’s in the Egg is unknown.

GB Sounds.summary: Use to listen to GameBoy era audio.
